title: Incentive measurement is delegated to the Core Council Risk Advisor, keeping the numbers out of the payer's and payee's hands
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.5.2.2.1.1.6 and A.6.1.1.3.2.5.2.2.2.1.6 both name "the Core Council Risk Advisor" as the Data Submission Responsible Actor for Keel's Kamino and Drift Integration Boosts. A.6.1.1.3.2.5.2.2.1.1.5 describes what that actor does: it "calculates the net deposits based on on-chain events and makes the data available through an API endpoint" at a fixed public URL.

The placement is the interesting part. Keel pays the boost and Kamino or Drift receives it, so both have a directional interest in the deposit figure — Keel to shrink it, the partner to inflate it. The Atlas gives the calculation to neither, assigning it instead to a Core-level advisor who sits outside the transaction and serves the ecosystem rather than the Agent.

Publication at a stable endpoint adds the second half of the guarantee: the number is not delivered privately to the payer but posted where the partner, KEEL holders and Operational GovOps can all read the same figure and recompute it from on-chain events if they disagree.

The residual exposure is a single point of dependency. The Atlas names one role and one URL, so an unavailable endpoint or a mistaken advisor stalls or misprices every Instance that inherits this parameter — a trade of counterparty bias for centralization of measurement.
description: For Keel's Integration Boosts, the Data Submission Responsible Actor is a Core-level role that computes net deposits from on-chain events and publishes them at a fixed public API endpoint.
